subject: POC evaluation plan, owners, and risk tracker - NovaHealth
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elliot Park <elliot.park@novahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood POC — aligning success criteria and risks

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo this morning — appreciate the clear walkthrough. A quick recap from our side and a few open items before we lock the POC plan: \n
1) Success criteria: we want to measure (a) <20% erroneous classification rate on our triage dataset, (b) average latency <= 250ms for 512-token requests, and (c) embedding similarity recall >= 92% for downstream search. Can you confirm Redwood can report these metrics at the token/route level?

2) Data flow: for the trial we will send sanitized de-identified payloads through your hosted endpoint in the us-west region. We need confirmation on data retention settings and option to disable logs for trial traffic.

3) Security artifacts: please share SOC 2 scope summary and any evidence that covers access controls and key management. Procurement will need this to move to an MSA.

4) Timeline & ownership: we are targeting a 3-week trial window starting the week of Dec 6. Samir will be our technical lead and procurement will own the contract. Who will own infra setup and triage on your side?

Open risks we flagged during the call: tokenizer edge-case on long clinical notes, and a potential discrepancy in prefix-caching behavior that might bias latency numbers. Would like these tracked so we can evaluate mitigations during the POC.

Can we get a short evaluation plan with owners and a live risk tracker before EOD Friday? Happy to jump on a quick alignment call if helpful.

Best,
Samira
Senior Product Manager, NovaHealth

Attachments: clinical-triage-sample.csv (text/csv)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novahealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood POC — aligning success criteria and risks

Samira — thanks for the recap and for the clear acceptance targets. Per your ask, I put together the evaluation plan and initial owner map below, and attached the trial-config.yaml plus a draft success-criteria workbook.

Evaluation plan (high level):
- Week 0 (Dec 6): infra & dataset ingestion (Redwood infra owner: Dylan)
- Week 1 (Dec 7–13): baseline runs, latency/accuracy benchmarking, quick health checks (owner: Sofia for quality measurement)
- Week 2 (Dec 14–20): targeted tuning (batching/quantization), KV cache validation, and rerun evaluation
- Week 3 (Dec 21–24): final acceptance window and handoff

Owners:
- Infra & endpoint setup: Dylan Brooks (dylan.brooks@redwood.ai)
- Quality metrics & eval harness: Sofia Ivanova (sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai)
- PM liaison & escalation: Jordan Blake (jordan.blake@redwood.ai)

Initial mitigations for risks you called out: we will instrument tokenizer edge-cases in the eval harness and add a synthetic stress set for long notes; we will also enable a prefix-KV cache audit to surface bias in latency sampling. If either causes >10% delta in acceptance metrics we will: (a) pause automated quantization, (b) switch to a host with full-precision fallback, and (c) escalate to our on-call infra lead.

Deliverables by Friday EOD:
- Shared success criteria workbook (attached)
- Live risk tracker (Jira SUP-321)
- Trial-config.yaml (attached)

Please confirm the start date and that Samir/Elliot have access to the staging endpoint once Dylan confirms setup. If you prefer, we can lock 30 minutes Thursday to run through the risk tracker together.

Thanks — Jordan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: trial-config.yaml (text/yaml), nova_poc_success_criteria.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood POC — aligning success criteria and risks

Looping in technical notes from infra perspective — I'll own setup and the first-run validation. Notes / immediate action items:

- Endpoint provisioning: staging cluster in us-west-2 provisioned; I'll follow up with ephemeral creds once certs are validated. ETA: Dec 4 EOD.
- Tokenizer mismatch: I reproduced the edge-case on our side with the quantized Llama-variant when feeding 6k+ character clinical notes. Tracker: SUP-321 — severity: medium-high. Root cause appears to be a byte-level normalization difference in the tokenizer preprocessor when truncation occurs.
- Mitigation plan: temporary workaround is to apply an aggressive pre-tokenization normalizer on client side (we can share a small lib) + run evaluation using the full-precision host. Longer term fix will be a tokenizer alignment patch scheduled for next engine sprint (target Jan 10).

Escalation path if SUP-321 blocks acceptance: 1) fallback to full-precision host (same model weights), 2) if still failing, engage Model Ops (SRE on-call: +1-555-0199), 3) product exception for extended trial window.

Also adding a quick smoke test checklist I will run post-provisioning: health check, tokenization diff report, 10-sample latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), and cache-hit ratio.

Dylan
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

Related link: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/SUP-321

From: Elliot Park <elliot.park@novahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@novahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood POC — aligning success criteria and risks

Jordan / Team — thanks, this looks good. A couple quick notes from procurement / technical ops: \n
- Procurement needs SOC 2 scope summary and contact for security questionnaires (please send by Thursday).
- We'd like the trial start confirmed for Dec 6, but if SUP-321 requires the host fallback we understand the timeline may shift — please flag asap.
- Can you add a link to a shared Confluence or Drive doc with the runbook and the acceptance workbook? That will help our auditors.

We approve the owner map as listed. Samira and I will review the success criteria workbook and push back if anything is unclear.

—Elliot
Director, Technical Operations — NovaHealth

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novahealth.com>, Elliot Park <elliot.park@novahealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood POC — aligning success criteria and risks

Thanks all — quick operational update: 

1) Dylan confirmed staging creds ETA Dec 4; endpoint will be in us-west-2.
2) I uploaded the success workbook to Drive and added read-only access for Samira/Elliot (link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d5e/view).
3) SOC 2 scope summary attached — security contact is Mira Shah (mira.shah@redwood.ai).
4) Risk tracker: SUP-321 created and assigned to Dylan; current status: "investigating". Mitigation requested: enable full-precision fallback and client pre-tokenizer during evaluation — Dylan will toggle if metrics show >10% divergence.

If SUP-321 becomes blocking during Weeks 1–2 we will escalate to Model Ops and propose a one-week extension of the trial window at no additional cost.

Next steps: Dylan will post provisioning confirmation; Sofia will post the first-run evaluation snapshot; Jordan will run weekly check-ins (Mon 10am PT). Please let me know if you need a different cadence.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-scope-summary.pdf (application/pdf)
